subject: Private deployment: risk carveouts, audit window and redline coordination
messages:
From: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmehealth.com>
To: vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc: samir.joshi@acmehealth.com, procure@acmehealth.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Private deploy redlines + requested audit window

Hi Vivek,

Thanks again for the call yesterday — Acme is excited about the private deployment option for our clinical inference workload. Our legal and procurement teams reviewed the MSA + Order Form and we have three core asks before we can move forward:

1) License boundary: request language that the runtime and model outputs are available only to Acme and that Redwood will not assert any retained rights over derivative models trained from Acme data.
2) Audit evidence: we need an agreed 2-hour audit window (remote) quarterly for 12 months and an inventory of artifacts (logs, snapshots) you can provide during that window.
3) Escrow-like fallback: in the event of termination for convenience or insolvency, we require a narrowly scoped deposit of runtime artifacts sufficient for business continuity for 90 days.

I attached our initial redlines (acme_redlines_initial.pdf) — these are higher-level asks; we expect Redwood to propose specific contract language. Can you confirm who on your side will own the legal sync and what timeline you can commit to for a redline pass?

Appreciate it —
Maya Patel
Senior Director, Strategic Sourcing
Acme Health
Attachments: acme_redlines_initial.pdf

---

From: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmehealth.com>
Cc: neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com, david.kim@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Sun, 30 May 2027 10:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Private deploy redlines + requested audit window

Maya — thanks for the clear list. I’ve looped in Neha (legal) for redlines, David (solutions) for operational feasibility of the audit window + artifacts, and Laura (privacy/regulatory) for the license boundary questions.

Plan:
- Neha will provide a first pass redline to your team by EOD Tue (2 business days).
- David will confirm what snapshot/log artifacts we can commit to provide during a remote 2-hour window and propose an evidence inventory template.
- Laura will review the proposed escrow-like fallback to align on minimum technical scope vs. IP exposure.

For clarity: Redwood’s position is to limit any runtime artifact deposit to what’s strictly necessary for Acme to run a fallback instance (operator runbook, image manifest, and a read-only artifact bundle). We generally avoid depositing model weights unless mutually agreed—we can propose an encrypted escrow that requires jointly held keys.

I’ll follow up with an internal timeline and attach our initial draft redlines.

Thanks,
Vivek Kulkarni
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
Redwood Inference

---

From: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>
To: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmehealth.com>, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc: david.kim@redwoodinference.com, laura.bennett@redwoodinference.com
Date: Tue, 1 Jun 2027 08:22:00 -0700
Subject: Draft redlines and evidence inventory (see attachments)

Maya — attaching our redlined MSA excerpt and a proposed Private Deployment Addendum. Key changes summarized below. Attachments: redlined_MSA_v1.docx, privdeploy_evidence_inventory.xlsx.

Summary of our proposed positions:
- License scope: we accept customer-exclusive runtime and output usage; we add explicit carveouts that Redwood retains pre-existing model IP and improvements to the runtime platform (operational code + optimizations). We propose language limiting derivative-model obligations — Redwood will not seek rights in models a customer trains independently using their data.

- Audit window & artifacts: we can commit to a quarterly remote 2-hour session for a 12-month period and provide an evidence inventory during the session:
  * service-level logs (request/response metadata, anonymized where required)
  * orchestration manifests and image digests
  * snapshot existence proofs (hashes) and signed manifests
  * operator runbook describing reboot/run steps
  * signed attestation from operations team (sample)

  We cannot provide live access to internal operator consoles or keys; instead we propose signed notarized artifacts and timed session demonstrations under an NDA and monitored screenshare.

- Escrow-like fallback: we propose a narrow fallback bundle that contains artifacts required to restore a runtime for 90 days, excluding model weights. If Acme requires model weights, that will be subject to a separate escrow agreement (encrypted deposit + dual-key release with escrow agent), and we’ll need to discuss costs and lead times.

Open items for negotiation (we flagged in the draft):
1) Definition of "derivative model" and guardrails around transfer of model snapshots.
2) Scope of attested artifacts vs. on-demand access during audit.
3) Insurance/indemnity carveouts tied to evidence-handling.

Next steps proposed by Redwood:
- We ask Acme to review our draft redlines and mark priority items in the attached document.
- Schedule a legal 30-minute sync (Samir + Neha) this week to close definitions; Vivek + David optional for ops questions.

Thanks — attaching the drafts now.

Best,
Neha Kapoor
Senior Counsel, Redwood Inference
Attachments: redlined_MSA_v1.docx, privdeploy_evidence_inventory.xlsx

---

From: Samir Joshi <samir.joshi@acmehealth.com>
To: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwoodinference.com>, vivek.kulkarni@redwoodinference.com
Cc: Maya Patel <maya.patel@acmehealth.com>, procure@acmehealth.com
Date: Mon, 31 May 2027 11:45:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Draft redlines and evidence inventory (see attachments)

Neha — thanks for the thoughtful draft and the quick turnaround. A few notes from Acme legal after a first pass:

1) We appreciate the carveout on model weights but need clarity on whether runtime artifact hashes + manifests are sufficient for our continuity plans. If hashes alone are acceptable, please document recovery testing we can rely on.

2) The proposed "notarized artifacts + monitored demo" approach is reasonable as a starting point, but Acme will insist on a pathway to escalate to in-person witnessing (limited) if remote artifacts are insufficient. Can Redwood propose a mutually agreeable escalation process and cost allocation?

3) For the definition of "derivative model": Acme needs a bright-line that models trained by Acme using Acme data are not subject to Redwood claims. We will push for an explicit warranty.

Action items for Redwood we need by EOD Wed:
- A short redline of the Addendum limited to 1 page of ‘commercial must-haves’ we can insert into the Order Form.
- Confirmation of whether Redwood will accept dual-key encrypted escrow for model weights (we expect Redwood to accept in principle with cost responsibilities assigned).
- Proposed escalation path (remote -> remote deep-dive -> on-site witness) and associated estimated costs for each stage.

If you prefer, we can take these offline over a 30-min call. Samir is available Wed 9–11am PT.

Regards,
Samir Joshi
Associate General Counsel
Acme Health
